ko.executive_summary: Major semiconductor companies are expanding HPC/AI infrastructure with new R&D centers and talent initiatives. NVIDIA and AMD are establishing R&D centers in South Korea and Taiwan respectively, while SK hynix is fundamentally restructuring its hiring process to prioritize AI-era capabilities, removing educational requirements and introducing half-day deep-dive interviews focused on reasoning skills. Marvell is doubling headcount with a $250 million investment in India.
key_facts: NVIDIA expanding AI efforts with new R&D center in South Korea
AMD setting up R&D center in Taiwan
SK hynix introducing half-day deep-dive interview format
SK hynix eliminating educational background restrictions in new hiring
SK hynix emphasizing AI competency assessment in recruitment
Marvell investing $250 million in India to double headcount over three years

implications.text: SK hynix's aggressive restructuring (performance bonuses in tens of millions, removal of credential barriers) signals intense competition for AI specialists across the HPC sector.
NVIDIA and AMD's Korea/Taiwan R&D centers indicate strategic commitment to proximity with manufacturing and regional talent ecosystems.
SK hynix's focus on reasoning and AI competency over academic credentials marks a fundamental realignment of hiring criteria toward domain-specific skills.
Marvell's India investment reflects broader industry trend of diversifying manufacturing and engineering footprint beyond traditional Taiwan/Korea hubs.

ko.counterpoint: Large-scale hiring announcements do not guarantee successful execution or long-term retention in an oversupplied AI talent market.
